title: Not yet (8.7)
hookLine: give me chastity and continency, only not yet
tomorrow: two verses, a garden, and a long 'not yet' ends. how?

cards: Every "I'll start Monday" has an ancestor in the Confessions. Augustine says that as a young man he prayed for a change and added a catch, and he writes the prayer down for anyone to read.
In the Pusey translation: "Give me chastity and continency, only not yet." He wanted the gift. Later.
It's almost funny, and it's also painfully honest: he could have left it out of the book, and he didn't.

teach.b: Why pray it that way? He says he was afraid God would hear him quickly, and heal him quickly, of a desire he'd rather keep fed than put out. So he hedged.
His excuses, in his Latin: modo, ecce modo, sine paululum. Soon.
Look, soon. Just a little while. And soon never came; a little while went on and on.
Notice what he doesn't say. He doesn't say never, and he doesn't pretend he didn't want the change.
Not yet isn't no. It keeps the prayer and the old life, both at once. That's yesterday's two wills, packed into one sentence.
Writing it down is part of the confession: the reader sees how far off he was, and what grace had to do.
Everything this week taught him, the spirit beyond the picture, the light above, Victorinus in the crowd, the monk of Egypt, he was holding at arm's length with two small words.

how: Catholics quote Augustine's 'only not yet' as an honest picture of putting off change, and the Church teaches that conversion is not a single moment but a turning that continues through a whole life.

o: a prayer that asks for change, but later
a refusal to ever ask God for anything
a promise to change on a set future date

games.q: the language of delay — tap the pairs.

s: Augustine hid his not-yet prayer and only admitted it late in life
he writes it into the Confessions himself, for anyone to read.
not yet let him keep the prayer and the old life at once
that's why it isn't quite no. it's yesterday's two wills in a sentence.
soon never came, he says; a little while went on and on.

games.q: a friend keeps saying she'll apologize to her sister "after finals." finals were a month ago. what does Augustine's not yet suggest?
o: not yet can be a quiet no; ask what it's protecting.
waiting is always wise; the right moment will come.
it proves she never meant to apologize at all.
games.why: Augustine's not yet kept both the prayer and the old life. He says soon never came, and he wrote that down so readers could see it.

practice: Rest your hands on your knees, palms open. Bring to mind one thing you've been saying not yet to, and for the length of the sit, just hold it there in open hands, without promising anything.

wordCard.voice: Not yet. Augustine's young prayer, honest to the point of embarrassing: yes, God, just later.

orig.note: Latin, Confessions 8.7: but not now, the end of Augustine's young prayer.

carryVoice: Only not yet: two small words that held a whole life in place. Another week, done.

sources.q: Give me chastity and continency, only not yet.
